content.thinking: I'm dropping the revision name from the root cause field. The second step of the chain cites ruled_out, which is fine, so I'll resubmit.

action_items.item: Add a CI test that runs the account-page spend calculations (lifetime, monthly and typical) against an account with a long purchase history, and fails when the work grows faster than linearly with the number of purchases. It should run on every change to src/io_shop.
Roll io-shop deployments out to a subset of replicas first, and hold the rest of the rollout until a latency check on that subset passes.
Link the HighLatency alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly. The response time of io-shop's slowest requests rose far above its usual level from the onset, while failed requests stayed within their normal variation.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 70dbcfde2b549d110a3817d92d60b6dd9786e78b. The metrics read back cover the hours from that deploy to the onset and show the service at its normal latency until the onset minute. The service was also measured back to normal once that revision was running again.
A feature-flag change. The flag provider's history showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before the investigation, and the change-event query returned no flags.

causal_chain.step: The slow requests started when io-shop began serving revision 5e07d73148d0a704b8fefe5f379bc652bb773655. It was deployed during the onset minute, and every replica was running it as of the deployment-status read.

That revision rewrote average_spend_per_item, which render_spend_summary uses for the account page whenever neither rollout flag is set. It now works out the lifetime total from the shopper's purchase list instead of dividing the total the account already carries.
The new loop re-sums the whole purchase list up to each position on every pass, so each account-page request does work that grows with the square of the shopper's purchase count.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change to how the shop works out a shopper's average spend made it add up the shopper's purchases again and again instead of once, so the work grew steeply with the number of things a shopper had bought.

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that checks how the cost of the account-page spend calculation grows with a long purchase history. The test the change added checks only the result, on an account with a short purchase list.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test running the calculation on a long purchase history would have shown the quadratic work before the revision was deployed, and the slow pages would never have reached shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No staged rollout was seen. The revision was running on every io-shop replica as of the deployment-status read, and no step was seen that served it to a slice of traffic and checked latency before the rest.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A canary with a latency check would have caught the slowdown on a small share of requests and stopped the rollout before every shopper's account page was affected.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read what the deployment of 5e07d73 changed, which pointed straight at the rewritten spend calculation.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found no flag changes by anyone else, which ruled out a flag change.
The Mitigation Agent rolled back the io-shop deployment, in a way that can be undone.
The Mitigation Agent watched the service and judged the rollback confirmed only after seeing it back below the incident's level.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #565 for a person to review.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person on call was brought in while the incident ran.

input.root_cause: The rewritten average_spend_per_item, the lifetime-average calculation the account page uses whenever neither rollout flag is set, works out the total from the purchase list instead of reading the total the account already carries. It does this by looping over the purchases and, on every pass, copying and re-summing the whole list up to that point. The work per request therefore grows with the square of the shopper's purchase count, even though only the last pass's sum is used.
input.still_at_risk: Account pages could slow down again if revision 5e07d73, or any later revision that still has its spend calculation, is deployed to io-shop.
input.symptom: Account pages on the shop loaded slowly
